candidates.title: SlimKV: Joint Token-Feature KV Cache Compression with Reconstruction-Free Beacon Attention
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
candidates.abstract: Long-context LLM serving is increasingly bottlenecked by KV-cache memory, especially in resource-constrained scenarios. Among existing KV-cache compression strategies, token-wise methods reduce cached states but risk information loss through eviction or condensation, while feature-wise methods reduce per-token KV dimensions but can require full-dimensional reconstruction to apply positional embedding, limiting decoding speedups. We introduce SlimKV, a question-agnostic joint token-feature KV-cache compression method. SlimKV uses low-rank-aware training to compress long contexts into beacon memory states with latent KV representations, together with layer-adaptive rank allocation. We further uncover a positional asymmetry: removing key-side RoPE affects beacon and raw tokens differently, with much smaller degradation for beacon tokens. Exploiting this asymmetry, SlimKV trains beacon KV projections under a K-RoPE-free constraint and enables latent-space attention during decoding, mitigating reconstruction latency. On LongBench, SlimKV outperforms baselines at 16x/32x compression and remains leading at 4x/8x, where it retains over 96% of the uncompressed model's score. Needle-in-a-Haystack confirms robustness across evidence positions, and efficiency evaluation shows up to 7.34x attention speedup and 3.38x end-to-end decoding speedup over the uncompressed model at 128K length.

candidates.reason: token削減と特徴次元削減を同時に行うKV圧縮。低rank-aware学習で長文脈をbeacon記憶へ集約し、layerごとにrankを割り当て、beacon keyに対するRoPEを外してlatent空間のままattentionを計算し復元遅延を避ける。著者要旨はLongBenchで4～32倍圧縮、128Kでattention最大7.34倍、end-to-end decode最大3.38倍を報告。KV容量と演算費用の直接的最適化としてaccept。

candidates.title: Long-Context Drafting Does Not Require Long-Context Drafters
candidates.abstract: Speculative decoding pairs a cheap drafter with parallel verification against the target. At ultra-long context it stops paying, because a drafter that attends over the full prefix inherits the target's context-dependent cost, so the speedup it was meant to provide first erodes and then reverses. The standard response is to build a long-context drafter, by training or fine-tuning one, or by using a multi-token-prediction head shipped inside the target checkpoint. We argue this is unnecessary, because the drafters in use are target-conditioned, reading hidden states the target computed over the entire prefix, so distant context already reaches them without their own attention, and verification corrects what they miss. We therefore freeze released short-context drafters and run them far past their training length under two inference-time mechanisms, one bounding the attention cache they see, which fixes their cost, and one re-basing their rotary position indices into the trained range. No weight is touched and the only tunable saturates early, so one vLLM-side configuration spans 4k to two million tokens, costing at most 0.16x of speedup at short length. We prove when a common index shift leaves the drafter's computation exactly unchanged, and decompose acceptance into two measurable gaps with sharp bounds. Whatever speedup a frozen drafter delivers at short context, it retains out to two million tokens, across three target-drafter pairs and five corpora. The claim concerns the flatness rather than the multiple, and removing either mechanism eliminates it. The gain is conditional on the speculative cost per emitted token staying below the matched target-only cost.
candidates.reason: 超長文脈でdraft側の全履歴attention費用が増えて投機復号の利益が失われる問題に対し、target hidden stateから長期情報を受け取るdraftは自身の長い履歴を必ずしも保持しなくてよいと主張する。既存の短文脈draftを凍結し、draft attention cacheの上限固定とRoPE位置の訓練範囲への再基準化を推論時だけ適用する。著者要旨は3組のtarget/draft・5コーパスで4K～200万tokenまで短文脈時のspeedupを維持すると報告。KV管理と投機復号の直接的方式としてaccept。

candidates.title: BS-Spec: BFP-Based Bit-Sharing for Self-Speculative LLM Decoding with LUT-Driven Mixed-Precision Acceleration
candidates.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across diverse inference services, serving workloads span a wide range of batch sizes, context lengths, and performance requirements. Speculative decoding improves inference throughput, but conventional approaches require a separate draft model and KV cache, while existing self-speculative methods suffer from workload-insensitive draft configurations and inefficient mixed-precision execution. In this paper, we present BS-Spec, a block floating point (BFP)-based bit-sharing framework that jointly optimizes draft construction, workload-aware precision selection, and hardware execution. BS-Spec derives multiple draft representations directly from a single BFP target model by partially loading the most significant bits of weights and the KV cache while preserving shared exponents, eliminating separate draft-model storage. Offline calibration selects the weight and KV-cache precision pair that maximizes estimated speedup for each serving regime, and a precision lookup table applies the selected configuration at runtime. To support this adaptive execution, we design a mixed-precision BFP accelerator with a lookup table (LUT)-based variable-precision datapath for both draft and target computation. Experimental results show that BS-Spec achieves up to $1.9\times$ speedup over conventional autoregressive decoding and improves speedup over the evaluated bit-sharing self-speculative decoding baselines by $67.2\%$ on average, demonstrating the benefits of jointly co-designing bit sharing, precision adaptation, and specialized hardware for diverse LLM serving workloads.
candidates.reason: 別draftモデルを持たずBFP target重みとKVの上位bitだけを部分読出しして複数精度のdraftを構成する。ワークロード別に最適な重み/KV精度を較正し、LUTを使う可変精度BFPアクセラレータでdraftとtargetを実行する。著者要旨は通常AR decode比最大1.9倍、比較対象のbit-sharing self-speculative方式より平均67.2%高いspeedupを報告。投機復号と専用hardwareの共同最適化としてaccept。
